# NSW public holidays

Check the NSW public holidays for 2026 and 2027. Learn about worker entitlements on these days.

![A man and a woman walking down a trail on a blue sky day surrounded by green grass and yellow flowers.](https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/styles/hero_l_x1/public/2025-08/snowy-mountains-mtb-walking.jpg?itok=vZ8fFZtE)

## NSW public holidays 2026 to 2027

| Holiday | 2026 | 2027 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Year's Day | Thursday 1 January 2026 | Friday 1 January 2027 |
| 3Additional Day | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| 2Australia Day | Monday 26 January 2026 | Tuesday 26 January 2027 |
| Good Friday | Friday 3 April 2026 | Friday 26 March 2027 |
| Easter Saturday | Saturday 4 April 2026 | Saturday 27 March 2027 |
| Easter Sunday | Sunday 5 April 2026 | Sunday 28 March 2027 |
| Easter Monday | Monday 6 April 2026 | Monday 29 March 2027 |
| Anzac Day | Saturday 25 April 2026 | Sunday 25 April 2027 |
| Additional Day | Monday 27 April 2026 | Monday 26 April 2027 |
| King's Birthday | Monday 8 June 2026 | Monday 14 June 2027 |
| 1Bank Holiday | Monday 3 August 2026 | Monday 2 August 2027 |
| Labour Day | Monday 5 October 2026 | Monday 4 October 2027 |
| Christmas Day | Friday 25 December 2026 | Saturday 25 December 2027 |
| 3Additional Day | Not applicable | Monday 27 December 2027 |
| Boxing Day | Saturday 26 December 2026 | Sunday 26 December 2027 |
| 3Additional Day | Monday 28 December 2026 | Tuesday 28 December 2027 |

_1 Retail bank branches and certain financial institutions are required to remain closed on the first Monday in August (Bank Holiday) **unless otherwise exempt** \- see_ [_Part 3A_](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2008/49/part3a) _of the_ [_Retail Trading Act 2008_](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/view/whole/html/inforce/current/act-2008-049) _. ‘Bank Holiday’ is included in this list because it has implications for the staffing of these institutions. See the_ [_Banks and Financial Institutions_](https://www.fairtrading.nsw.gov.au/trades-and-businesses/business-essentials/information-for-specific-industries/retail-trading) _page of the Fair Trading website. The **Bank Holiday is not a declared public holiday**._

2 _The public holiday standard in the_ [_Public Holidays Act 2010_](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115) _provides that when Australia Day (26 January) falls on a Saturday or Sunday, there will be no public holiday on that day and instead the following Monday is to be the public holiday._

_3The public holiday standard in the Act provides that when New Year's Day, Christmas Day or Boxing Day falls on a Saturday or Sunday there is to be an additional public holiday on the following Monday or Tuesday._

### Public holidays in NSW legislation

[Section 4](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115/part2/sec4) of the [_Public Holidays Act 2010_](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115) (the Act) declares the standard public holidays that apply in NSW.

[Section 5](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115/part2/sec5) of the Act provides for the declaration of additional public holidays including public holidays for a part of the State.

[Section 8](https://www.legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115/part3/sec8) of the Act provides for the declaration of a local event day in a local government area.

Note that the declaration of a local event day does not make the local event day a public holiday.

## Additional public holiday information

Expand allCollapse all

NSW local public holidays or local event days
keyboard\_arrow\_down

In addition to these standard public holidays for all of NSW, there are also some [Local Public Holidays](https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/public-holidays/local-public-holidays "Local public holidays in NSW") and [Local Event Days](https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/public-holidays/local-event-days "Local Event Days in NSW") declared in regional and rural NSW to recognise a significant annual event for the local community like an agricultural show or racing carnival.

These occasions may be declared by the Minister for Industrial Relations following an application made by a local council for a whole day or part of a day.

- [Local Public Holidays](https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/public-holidays/local-public-holidays "Local public holidays in NSW")
- [Local Event Days](https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/public-holidays/local-event-days "Local Event Days in NSW")

Retail shop and bank trading restrictions
keyboard\_arrow\_down

Ask about trading restrictions and exemptions for banks and retail shops by calling Fair Trading NSW at [13 32 20](tel: 13 32 20).

You can also see [Trading on public holidays page](https://www.fairtrading.nsw.gov.au/trades-and-businesses/business-essentials/information-for-specific-industries/retail-trading) on Fair Trading NSW website.

Workplace rights and responsibilities for national system employers and employees
keyboard\_arrow\_down

Public holidays, including local public days, will affect workplace entitlements for national system employers and employees. Information is provided by the Fair Work Ombudsman on the [National Employment Standards for public holidays](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/tools-and-resources/fact-sheets/minimum-workplace-entitlements/public-holidays) and in the awards and agreements that apply to your workplace.

The [Public Holidays Act 2010](https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115 "Public Holidays Act 2010 (https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115)") notes that the following provisions of the [Fair Work Act 2009](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text "Fair Work Act 2009 (https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text)") of the Commonwealth also apply to employees and employers in NSW.

- Section 114, about the entitlement to be absent from employment on a public holiday, and
- Section 116, about payment for absence on a public holiday.

For information and assistance, contact the [Fair Work Ombudsman](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ "Fair Work Ombudsman website (https://www.fairwork.gov.au/)").

Essential guides
keyboard\_arrow\_down

### NSW Guide to Public Holidays

How you can prepare your business:

- Get to know which public holidays may affect your business.
- Ensure you have a leave calendar or a staff log of available staff.
- Find out about the Industrial Relations implications and obligations for staff working on a Public Holiday, for example, loading or penalty.
- Take time to understand what additional staffing needs may be required

Access the:

[NSW Guide to Public Holidays](https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/public-holidays/public-holiday-resources "NSW Public Holiday Guide and Presentation for employers") and [NSW Industrial Relations public holiday presentation](https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/public-holidays/public-holiday-resources "NSW Public Holiday Guide and Presentation for employers").

![Two co-workers sitting in coffee shop working on digital tablet smiling.](https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/styles/content_x1/public/2026-01/public-holiday-employee-block.jpg?itok=pFm_viQb)

### Employer and employee essentials

To find information on public holiday entitlements, employers and employees should check their industrial instrument, for example, award, agreement, or employment contract. They should also refer to the [National Employment Standards](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/national-employment-standards) in the [Fair Work Act 2009](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text "Fair Work Act 2009 (https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text)").

## Public Holiday FAQs

Expand allCollapse all

1\. What are the public holidays in NSW?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

Holidays for NSW are gazetted under the [Public Holidays Act 2010](https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115 "Public Holidays Act 2010 (https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115)"). They are statewide or regional public holidays and apply to all businesses across NSW.

The standard public holidays across NSW include:

- New Year’s Day
- Australia Day
- Good Friday
- Easter Saturday
- Easter Sunday
- Easter Monday
- Anzac Day
- King’s Birthday
- Labour Day
- Christmas Day
- Boxing Day.

2\. What is a local or regional public holiday?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

Local public holidays may also be declared in regional and rural NSW. They are holidays that commemorate a day of special significance to a specific local community. These are in addition to the standard public holidays that apply to the whole of NSW.

Note: A local public holiday is a declared public holiday for that area for work purposes. Additional penalty payments may apply. Refer to your applicable industrial instrument for details.

3\. What is a Local Event Day?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

There are a small number of Local Event Days that can be for a whole day or part of a day. These are in addition to standard public holidays that apply to the whole of NSW. They might be for an event like an agricultural show or racing carnival.

Importantly, Local Event Days are not a declared public holiday for work purposes.

4\. What is an Additional Day?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

Every few years, New Year's Day, Christmas Day or Boxing Day falls on a Saturday or Sunday. When this happens, there will be an additional gazetted public holiday on the following available weekday.

5\. Is a Bank Holiday a declared public holiday?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

No, it is not a declared public holiday for all of NSW. Only retail bank branches and certain financial institutions are required to remain closed on the first Monday in August, unless otherwise exempt.

For more information refer to the [NSW Fair Trading website](https://www.fairtrading.nsw.gov.au/).

6\. When is Anzac Day public holiday observed?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

The Anzac Day holiday is always recognised and observed on the 25 April every year. This includes when it falls on a weekend.

7\. What about the Australia Day public holiday?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

Where Australia Day falls on a weekend, there is no public holiday on that day. Instead, the following Monday is the public holiday.

8\. Do I get extra pay to work on a public holiday?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

In most cases an employee that works on a gazetted public holiday is entitled to extra payment. This is usually in the form of an additional penalty or loading.

Detailed information on public holiday entitlements is in your workplace industrial instrument. This could be an award, agreement or employment contract that covers your workplace.

For information on pay and conditions of employment in the national system visit the [Fair Work Ombudsman website](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ "Fair Work Australia").

If you work in the NSW Local Government industry, visit our [Local Government Industry page](https://www.industrialrelations.nsw.gov.au/industries/local-government/ "Local government - industrial relations information (https://www.industrialrelations.nsw.gov.au/industries/local-government/)"). You can also call us on [131 628](tel: 131 628) for help with public holidays.

9\. Do employees get paid for a public holiday that they do not work?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

In most cases where an employee is off work on a public holiday, and that day is their regular working day, the employee would still be entitled for payment for the absence on a public holiday.

The [Public Holidays Act 2010](https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115 "Public Holidays Act 2010 (https://legislation.nsw.gov.au/#/view/act/2010/115)") also notes that the following provisions of the [Fair Work Act 2009](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text "Fair Work Act 2009 (https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2009A00028/latest/text)") also apply to employees and employers in NSW:

- Section 114, about the entitlement to be absent on a public holiday, and
- Section 116, about payment for absence on a public holiday.

Please refer to the relevant industrial laws and instruments including the specific Award or Agreement that covers your workplace for detailed information on public holiday entitlements.

For information on pay and conditions of employment in the national system, visit the [Fair Work Ombudsman website](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ "Fair Work Australia").

10\. What if a public holiday occurs while I am on Long Service Leave?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

You may have a situation where you are on [Long Service Leave](https://www.nsw.gov.au/employment/rights-responsibilities/leave/long-service-leave "Long service leave") when a gazetted public holiday occurs. If this is a normal working day for an employee, an extra day must be added to the Long Service Leave period.

11\. Where to get more information on NSW public holidays?
keyboard\_arrow\_down

For information on pay and conditions of employment in the national system, visit the [Fair Work Ombudsman website](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ "Fair Work Australia").

For information on pay and conditions of employment in the national system, please visit the [Fair Work Ombudsman website](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ "Fair Work Australia").

For any NSW business trading hours information on public holidays (including Bank Holiday information) visit the [NSW Fair Trading website](https://www.fairtrading.nsw.gov.au/ "NSW Fair Trading (https://www.fairtrading.nsw.gov.au/)").
